title: Patterns
text: A pattern is an expression in which some parts are wildcards, written with a ~. Anything else in a pattern, such as a function name or a number, must appear in the subject as written.

title: Wildcards
text: wildcardmatches~xone argument~!xone argument, or a default value when there is none~~xzero or more arguments, bound as a tuple~~~xone or more arguments, bound as a tuple A pattern can have only one wildcard of a given name, so ~x + ~~x is not allowed. A name may be repeated, though, in which case …

title: Slots
text:
The slot ~x matches a single argument, which may itself be an expression: julia> CPM._match(:(~x + ~y), :(a + sin(b)))
Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any} with 2 entries:
  :y => :(sin(b))
  :x => :a

julia> CPM._match(:(~x + ~x), :(a + a))
Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any} with 1 entry:
  :x => …

title: Default slots
text:
The default slot ~!x matches as ~x does, but when there is no argument to match it binds a default value: 0 within a sum, and 1 within a product, or as an exponent or denominator. julia> CPM._match(:(~x + ~!y), :(a + b))
Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any} with 2 entries:
  :y => :b
  :x => :a

title: Segments
text:
The segment ~~x matches any number of arguments, including none, and binds them as a tuple. The segment ~~~x is the same, but must match at least one argument. julia> CPM._eachmatch(:(~x + ~~y), :(a + b + c))
4-element Vector{Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any}}:

title: Guards
text:
A wildcard may have a guard, a predicate its value must satisfy, written ~x::pred. The match is made only when pred(value) returns true. A guard which returns anything else, or throws an error, rejects the match. julia> CPM._match(:((~x)^(~n::isinteger)), :(x^2))
Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any} …

title: Where a guard is found
text: In a quoted pattern, a guard given by name, or an expression for a guard, is evaluated in Main (with names looked up in Main, then Base) when the pattern is first matched. title: CommutativePatternMatching.Rule
text: Rule A rule created by @rule. Call it on a subject to rewrite it: rule(sub) returns the rewritten term, or nothing if sub does not match.

title: CommutativePatternMatching._eachmatch
text: Tuple{Any, Any} _eachmatch(pat, sub) Return a vector of the matches of the pattern pat to the subject sub, each a dictionary from wildcard names to their values. The vector is empty if there is no match.

title: CommutativePatternMatching._match
text: Tuple{Any, Any} _match(pat, sub) Return the first match of the pattern pat to the subject sub, or nothing if there is no match. See _eachmatch.

title: CommutativePatternMatching._rewrite
text: Tuple{Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any}, Any} _rewrite(σ, rhs, [S]) Rewrite the template rhs using the match σ. If rhs is a function, it is called on σ, as for a rule from @rule. title: CommutativePatternMatching.@pattern
text: Tuple{Any} @pattern expr Create a pattern from expr, as :(expr) would, except each guard of a wildcard (~x::pred, ~~x::pred, ~~~x::pred) is evaluated where the macro is called and spliced into the pattern as a value. A guard in a quoted pattern, :(~x::isfoo), is looked up by name in Main and Base …

title: The @rule macro
text: The @rule macro creates a rule, lhs => rhs. The left-hand side is a pattern, as for @pattern. Calling the rule on a subject returns rhs, with each wildcard replaced by its value in the first match, or nothing when the subject does not match. julia> r = @rule sin(2 * ~x) => 2 * sin(~x) * …

title: Differences from SymbolicUtils
text: The wildcards ~x, ~!x and ~~x, guards written ~x::pred, and the form @rule lhs => rhs are as in SymbolicUtils, and both try the arguments of + and * in different orders.
